quotes.text: This technology has the potential to pose an existential risk to our economy and to humanity itself. This is one of the most pressing issues that our country needs to face, and we need to create federal oversight and regulation of this industry now!
We need federal laws saying that they cannot build these things, these AI companies, until and unless they can prove that they’re going to provide all their own power.

It’s a technology that is, quite literally, the biggest existential threat we are facing as a country, I think. I mean, this artificial intelligence technology is something that the developers are saying could have a 10-20 percent chance of having catastrophic harm to all of humanity in the next ten years, if we don’t get our arms around it.

This is the technology that, on the one hand, could cure cancer. But on the other, it could kill all of humanity. [...] And I will work like hell to make sure we actually get our arms around it, that we have back-end access to this technology so we can pull the plug on it if it poses a risk to all of us.

“Every week there’s more distressing information about these artificial intelligence models,” he said. “They’re finding inside of bank accounts, doing things that the creators of this tech did not actually ask.”

The industry driving these data centers, artificial intelligence, is perhaps the biggest existential threat to our economy, to working people. [...] It is technology that has the biggest potential to further consolidate immense, terrifying amounts of power in the hands of even fewer people.

The technology itself, I think gets lost in this conversation, how terrifying this technology that could end all of humanity is. We’ve read (this in) sci-fi novels. Now we’re living through them and no one’s doing anything.
AI tech poses a existential risk to all of humanity if you don't believe me just listen to the executives of these tech companies,

My position has been the same since the beginning of this campaign. We need legislation saying Artificial Intelligence cannot be in (new) data centers until or unless we have guarantees they are not going to suck up our power, our water, come in and use cheap labor, denigrate our open spaces.

Artificial Intelligence companies that are running roughshod right now with zero regulation and with, in fact, reverse regulation from the federal ... are perhaps the scariest single existential threat to our country and the future of our economy.
No one seems to be scared enough about this that they’re doing anything at the federal level, and that’s the bigger fight to have,

An AI Super PAC poured $590,000 into Montana to elect their very own political puppet, AI Aaron, just in the month of May. 

AI Aaron will serve the corporations who fund his campaign & pull his strings. We’ve got plenty of political puppets in Washington, let’s not send another. https://t.co/Xr8QRdeyNx
Meanwhile, my opponent Aaron Flint is supported by an AI-backed Super PAC thats spending millions trying to buy him a seat in Congress.

Yesterday, the CEO of one of the world's biggest AI companies admitted his own technology is moving too fast to be safe. Last week, a lead researcher at that same company quit, warning that AI companies are "gambling with our lives" and that it "could kill us all"

In Congress, I'll fight for real oversight of AI and work to pass bills that protect us and regulate this industry. This is too urgent for Congress to sit on vacation. And it's too important to let a political puppet for AI companies represent Montana. https://t.co/HDIcmkL5kd

AI and the data centers that these AI companies are building is the single biggest existential threat I see us having to address in Congress here. [...] I will fight for serious regulation and oversight of that AI tech, of those companies, making sure we put a kill switch into the models that they're building so we can pull the plug on those things if they pose a threat to entire industries and to all of us as a species.

We need to regulate these companies. We need to pass bills like the Kill Switch Act to make sure that we can pull the plug on this technology if it poses a threat to all of us. And we need to make sure that we require third-party verification that these models are safe, because right now they're not.

Right now, Congress is full of politicians who answer to corporations and high dollar donors, while working people fall further behind. That’s what we’re up against in this race, where my opponent has over $6 million of spending from corporate donors, AI companies, and SuperPACs.

110+ students at Montana State came to our town hall today! We talked about regulating AI, protecting public lands, the power of unions, and our broken system of campaign finance. 

Thank you for coming out, Cats! Vote, volunteer, and tell your friends about what you heard today! https://t.co/23tFm8Xm48

And in the last few days, my opponent has been spamming Montanans with an A.I.-generated deepfake ad—partly because he can’t find any real people who agree with his platform, and partly to demonstrate his loyalty to A.I. executives.
